one_liner: AGPL header-only C++23 static kd-tree for low-dimensional points (3D default); median 3.7x faster builds and 1.9x faster k-NN than nanoflann.
what_it_does: kd3 builds a static, bucketed kd-tree over 'fat points' (coordinates plus a uint32 payload id) and answers exact 1-NN, nearest squared distance, k-NN into a caller-supplied buffer, and ray or 'thick ray' (cylinder) intersection queries. KdTree<limits<float>, cfg_t{...}> owns the arrays; queries run through a trivially copyable, non-owning KdTreeView over std::span, which suits GPU offload and memory-mapped storage. Build options (leaf_size, has_aabb, has_payload) are template parameters, errors come back as std::expected, and there is an STB-style C API (kd3-c.h) and an experimental GLSL generator. It is not a nanoflann drop-in: no dataset adaptor, no radius search, no incremental updates, and build() reorders the input span.
how_it_is_fast: Leaves are fixed-size buckets stored structure-of-arrays (coords[D][leaf_size], aligned to the SIMD width), so distances are computed for a whole bucket in vectorizable loops; the default leaf size is 4x the detected SIMD lane count (32 floats on AVX2). Internal nodes are an implicit array of split values with split dimensions bit-packed into 64-bit words, and the tree size is fixed up front from n / leaf_size, so the build is std::nth_element median partitioning into preallocated arrays, run as OpenMP tasks above 10,000 points. Queries use a bounded stack (96 entries) with no heap allocation. The optional has_aabb stores a tight box per subtree, so queries far from the data prune whole subtrees, and has_payload = NONE drops ids for a distance-only 1-NN path.
when_to_use: Static 2-4D point clouds (LiDAR tiles, scanned meshes, surflets for SDF raymarching) with 10^5-10^7 points, queried at high rates for 1-NN or small-k k-NN.

Queries that lie on or near the data, such as k-NN graphs, ICP-style correspondence or jittered samples: the 5950X CSV shows on-cloud k=10 with the base config at a median 1.73x nanoflann and 1-NN at 2.21x.
Queries spread through empty space, provided you enable has_aabb: aabb configurations reach a median 1.68x (k=10) and 2.23x (1-NN) on bbox-volume queries, where the base config loses.
Pipelines that rebuild the tree often on many cores: OpenMP task build, median 3.7x faster than nanoflann given the same thread count.
Ray, cylinder or nearest-distance queries that must also run in a shader (GLSL generator) or from C via kd3-c.h, and AGPL-3.0 (or a negotiated licence) is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: Closed-source or SaaS products without a separate licence from the author: AGPL-3.0-only network copyleft.

Base or fast configurations with queries spread through the volume: in the CSV they are slower than nanoflann in 10 of 11 (k-NN base), 9 of 11 (1-NN base) and 8 of 11 (1-NN fast) datasets, down to 0.013x on synthetic-anisotropic 1-NN.
Small clouds where build time matters: on bunny (35,947 points) every kd3 configuration builds slower than nanoflann (about 11.4 ms vs 2.5 ms for base, 0.22x).

Radius or range search, dynamic insert/delete, high-dimensional data (>4D), or compilers without C++23 (std::expected, std::span): kd3 offers only 1-NN, k-NN, nearest distance and ray queries on a static tree; nanoflann or Pkd-tree (batch updates) fit those cases better.
Projects needing a mature, widely deployed library: 11 stars, 38 commits, first stable release July 2026.

integration.form: header-only (include/kd3/*.hpp); optional static lib and STB-style C interface (kd3-c.h); xmake package, and release tarballs of the headers
integration.dependencies: C++ standard library (nth_element, sort, vector, span, expected) and OpenMP (or the author's omp-stub for serial builds); the benchmarks additionally need nanoflann and LASlib/lastools
integration.min_toolchain: C++23 (xmake set_languages cxx23/c23); README notes GCC 15/16 miscompile at -O2 (see gotchas)
integration.platforms: any C++23 target; SIMD width auto-detected (AVX-512, AVX/AVX2, SSE2/SSE4.2, or std::simd), override with KD3_SIMD_PARALLELISM; built for -march=native by default, so no binary releases
integration.thread_safety: not documented; queries are const noexcept on an immutable view, so concurrent queries on a built tree look safe (inferred from source), and the build itself is OpenMP-parallel
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — covers nanoflann's static-index KNN (k-NN and 1-NN) for low-dimensional float points, but with a different API (FatPoint arrays and payload ids instead of a dataset adaptor), no radiusSearch, no dynamic index, and it reorders the input

gotchas: The headline 5.05x maximum comes from the 'fast' configuration (has_payload = NONE, query_distance2_inline), which returns only the nearest squared distance and not which point, while nanoflann's figure includes the index; compare against the base or aabb rows for like-for-like k-NN.

The default leaf_size and bucket alignment follow the compile-time SIMD width (and KD3_SIMD_PARALLELISM is #undef'd after use), so the memory layout of a 'memory-mapped' tree depends on the flags it was built with; the C header hard-codes KD3_LEAF_SIZE 32 with a TODO.

The README's known issue: GCC 15 and 16 at -O2 can emit an aligned movaps to an unaligned address in Builder::build's leaf-fill loop, crashing on tiny trees; the author attributes it to a compiler bug.

The benchmark and the release builds use -ffast-math with -march=native (xmake 'native' option, on by default); to reproduce the nanoflann comparison you must configure with both --with_evaluation=true and --with_demo=true, because KD3_BENCH_NANOFLANN is only defined under with_demo, although docs/benchmarking.md shows only the first flag.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Over nanoflann and PicoTree when the data is 3D, static and queried far more often than rebuilt, you can enable has_aabb, and AGPL is acceptable; otherwise nanoflann or PicoTree (also catalogued, about 2.6x faster builds than nanoflann) are the safer defaults, and Pkd-tree fits when you need parallel batch updates. Unlike Janos95/kdtree, kd3 checks every benchmark row against brute force.
verified_claims_summary: The author's comparative benchmark (benchmarks.comparative.cpp: 100,000 queries per row, one timed pass, every row checked against brute force) ran on a '5950X' workstation with an unstated compiler, built for both libraries with xmake's 'fastest' optimisation plus -march=native -ffast-math. kd3's build is a median 3.68x faster than nanoflann's (leaf size 10, same OpenMP thread count), and its single-threaded query throughput a median 1.86x higher across 132 rows on 11 datasets. 39 rows are slower than nanoflann, mostly base or fast configurations on volume queries; the has_aabb configurations (aabb and fast-aabb, 66 rows) are slower in only 9.
status_note: Active (v1.3.1 on 2026-09-23, five releases since July 2026) but young and small; AGPL-3.0, so copyable only into AGPL-compatible projects, with a different licence available from the author on request.
